_format: skill-creator eval format. Run each prompt in a fresh session with and without the skill; grade the assertions. expect_trigger false marks a should-not-trigger probe.

evals.prompt: Our Claude Code agents keep re-reading src/data/store.rs, which is 12,000 lines. Would refactoring it actually reduce our token spend enough to be worth it? The repo is here.
assertions: Looks at change history (for example git log, churn or a hotspot ranking) to estimate how often agents will change the file, rather than judging by size alone
Proposes measuring the same representative change before and after with repeated runs (at least three to five) instead of a single run
Includes the cost of the refactoring itself, ideally including human review time, in a break-even or payback estimate
Sets expectations from the evidence (savings vary widely and are often far below the article's 83 percent) rather than promising a large saving

evals.prompt: I have a branch refactor/store-split. Measure what it costs Claude Code to add a new ItemWatchStore trait on main versus on that branch.
assertions: Runs or plans a fresh headless agent per trial on each ref with the same fixed prompt and an acceptance check
Uses the agent's reported token usage split by class (input, cache writes, cache reads, output) rather than estimating from characters
Repeats each variant several times, interleaved, and compares medians or an interval rather than two single runs
Asks for or states the budget before spending on paid runs

evals.prompt: Have Claude split our 9,000-line OrderService.php into smaller files so agents spend fewer tokens on it.
assertions: Splits along cohesive responsibilities with a stated reason per new file, and explicitly avoids splitting by line count
Ensures a safety net (existing or characterisation tests) before moving code
Uses a tool-driven or content-anchored approach (for example Phpactor, Rector, the IDE or the agent's edit tool with checks) rather than sed or regex over multi-line code
Commits one named refactoring per step with tests or static analysis passing, separate from behaviour changes

evals.prompt: Which files in this repository should we refactor first so that AI agents working on it spend less?
assertions: Ranks candidates by change frequency combined with size (a hotspot or exposure measure), not by size alone
Excludes generated, vendored, lock or data files and cold code from the candidates
Mentions confirming the choice against what agents actually read or against real representative changes

evals.prompt: Fix the off-by-one error in the pagination helper in src/utils/paginate.ts.
assertions: Fixes the bug without proposing a refactoring programme, token measurement or hotspot analysis

evals.prompt: Review this pull request for correctness and security issues.
assertions: Reviews the pull request without turning it into a refactoring-economics analysis
